independenceStatement: I independently inspected only /tmp/skillpilot-a2/k4-blind-v2 and created this result outside that packet. I read its candidate, task/marking, rubric, instructions, scope and all 20 DE/EN submissions; I opened the actual quantitative stimulus and every referenced drawing R01-R10 and measured the images against their drawn rulers. I did not inspect repository material, author/expected-score records, other editions, previous marker results, the other marker, or reconciliations; I did not obtain or share marks with another reviewer. The parent was only told that input inspection was complete. No learner results were written. No memory or external sources were consulted.

releaseDecision.note: Scientifically and pedagogically releasable for the narrow declared velocity-arrow assessment. S06 can be clarified for exact numerical reproducibility and S14 label can be cleaned up; neither changes its fail outcome. External target-goal full wording and actual curricular/runtime activation are not present in this blind evidence.

findings.finding: The actual stimulus has A at x=70 px and B at x=610 px, aligned with ruler 0 and 3 cm: 180 px per drawn cm. Its velocity arrow runs A to B; the last blue pixels are partly covered by B, not evidence of a different length. Thus initial length is 3 cm, speed 6 m/s, object separation 3 m. II must have 2 drawn cm, ending 1 cm before B. Image measurements agree with the solution.

The task is scientifically correct, clearly requests a real drawing, and uses scale change to distinguish the velocity quantity from position-space distance and from tip contact. The simple products/quotients and point sketch are suitable for prepared lower-secondary learners, including year 6 with prior velocity/unit teaching. No abstract vector-space formalism is needed. Actual chat drawing submission and renderer behavior remain host acceptance, not proved by this content review.

The four 4-point weights and 13.5 pass mark prevent any wholly absent core compensated by the other performances: 1+4+4+4=13. All four supplementary-only patterns are present (S06 A, S07/S12 B, S08 C, S03 D) and fail. A maintained misconception worth zero can total at most 12. No extra pass gate was introduced.

A correct drawing/length cannot pass without tip interpretation: S03 totals 13 despite prediction and invariance; S20 totals 12 with the entire D response absent. S17/S18 also total 12 for maintained D misconceptions. S19 correctly receives 16 after explicit retraction.

Minor-slip policy is applied at its origin exactly once. S02/S10 isolated unit/legend slips and S13 arithmetic plus copied drawing consequence each total 15.5. S11 omitted head with independent rightwards evidence totals 15.5; S07/S12 omitted heads without direction evidence each total 13. S04 is 14; S05 combines two independent 0.5 slips with a missing 1.5 D reason and passes exactly at 13.5. Dropping another independent 0.5 would yield 13 and fail.

A supplement asks for a property explanation linked to why the arrow starts at the carrier. S06 gives only the generic property sentence, not an explicit therefore-starts-there link. I grant the available 1 supplementary point for that conceptual property evidence, without reconstructing any carrier/placement core; a strictly conjunctive reading could give A=0 and total=12. Either reading fails. Minimal repair: make S06 state the generic causal rule explicitly, while retaining the unnamed carrier and unplaced application, or specify that merely naming property earns this supplement. This is a numerical reproducibility caveat, not a pass/fail ambiguity.

R05 starts at B but labels the arrow v_A, while the text unequivocally maintains carrier B under a wrong rule. Maintained misconception still forces A=0, so no scoring ambiguity under the stated rubric. Minimal case cleanup would label this arrow v_B; do not charge the mismatch a second time.

German and English task, scoring rules and all 20 written submissions are substantively equivalent. I independently read both and assign identical points in every language. Case explanations use the actual drawings, not an assumed intended drawing.

This review approves the narrow declared assessment behavior: assign velocity carrier/origin, read direction/magnitude, redraw at a new velocity scale, and explain the non-position/non-contact meaning of the tip. The supplied bundle names the external covered goal by ID only; it does not reproduce that goal full text. Exact coverage of any additional requirements in that external goal, official jurisdiction claims, actual 42-view activation, or runtime handoffs cannot be certified from this blind packet.
